title: Ernest Rapanya's career and duplex snare drum
summary: He describes Rapanya as a cabaret drummer and his aluminum duplex snare, now used by Alfred Williams.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Can you tell us any more about Ernest Rapania? We don't hear too much about him.

Well, Ernest Rapania was a drummer working every cabaret around New Orleans. He, right after World War I, he was a veteran of World War I, and right after all, he worked at a place for years who was known as the hummingbird, I believe, which is beyond Franklin, between Bionerville and Iberville, form of the old district. He worked there for many years.
Can you remember anything about his outfit, his drums and so on?

Well, I do know he had, in the line of a snare, he had, and it's still being used today, if I'm not mistaken by Alfred, was a duplex snare drum. Looked like it was all lumen, a duplex snare drum. Alfred Williams, you think? I think he still has it. I think he has a duplex. I forgot. Yeah, well, that used to be on the Strapanius drum.
He might have told us that. I forgot.

Yeah, because I'm sure Alfred had that drum. I used it several times in some parades in the lately years with Poissy Huffer. Yeah, I've seen that drum. Yeah, when I used to relief Alfred sometimes and he'd be feeling bad.
I didn't know they made aluminum drums that far back.
Yeah, it was a lumen snare drum. Now, I couldn't remember what sort of a bass drum on his head, but it was a regular, you know, a regular bass, wood shell bass drums, separated tensions.
Yeah, the two rods and something.
